title: The browser is the source of truth
summary: A concise presenter journey connecting loaded code, live runtime behavior, authenticated traffic and transient SPA state.

chapters.title: Connect code, runtime and dependency evidence
chapters.summary: A support widget looks like one feature in the browser, while three evidence families explain different parts of its security posture.
presenterSteps: Open the review target and identify the dependency loaded with the widget.
Review the browser-message handler before triggering the prepared reply.
Send the reply, correlate the live DOM behavior, and compare the repaired target.

evidence.observation: The loaded client dependency and its deployed version.
The message trust check and DOM update visible in client code.
The browser-message value reaching the live DOM operation.

chapters.browserAdvantage: The browser connects the dependency that actually loaded, the handler shipped to the page and the runtime path the user exercised.

checkpoint.prompt: Which explanation uses the complete browser evidence?

options.label: Loaded dependency, static handler and live DOM behavior describe one feature.
The dependency version alone proves every runtime path.
The visible markup alone explains the message trust boundary.

chapters.title: Test the request the application really sends
chapters.summary: An order-search request exists only after the browser establishes scoped state and submits the application's form workflow.
presenterSteps: Open the review workflow through the local route-aware server and establish its scoped session.
Submit the normal order search so the browser creates the form-encoded POST request.
Use active DAST on the captured request, then repeat the workflow against the repaired API.

evidence.observation: The exact same-origin POST, parameters and server response behavior.
The scoped session and request context required by the endpoint.

chapters.browserAdvantage: The browser supplies the authenticated request shape and session context that a host-root crawl or invented request does not reproduce.

checkpoint.prompt: Why should the captured browser request be the DAST baseline?

options.label: It preserves the method, encoding, parameters and scoped session used by the application.
A request to the host root always represents every authenticated form.
Changing the request to an unauthenticated GET provides the same coverage.

chapters.title: Catch evidence that exists for milliseconds
chapters.summary: A same-document route change creates meaningful DOM behavior for only a brief interval before the application clears it.
presenterSteps: Open the review target with static and runtime analysis ready before the interaction.
Trigger the route action and observe the same-document URL change without a reload.
Correlate the short-lived DOM evidence with active testing, then compare the allow-listed repaired route.

evidence.observation: The route-reading code and DOM operation present in the shipped script.
The live route value reaching the transient DOM update.
The active browser route mutation and observable execution evidence.

chapters.browserAdvantage: A browser-aware scanner observes same-document navigation and short-lived DOM state that may disappear before a later page snapshot.

checkpoint.prompt: What makes this SPA evidence easy to miss?

options.label: It appears after same-document navigation and survives for only a short interval.
It exists permanently in the initial server response after every full reload.
It depends on an uncontrolled external service.
